summary: Raise both sides to the power f (the number of infinite places of E). Then σ(s₀)^f = σ(χ_fin(α))⁻¹, and a power χ_fin(α)^k is a norm from E to K, so σ fixes it and |σ(χ_fin(α))| = |χ_fin(α)|. The absolute value of χ_fin(α) is the inverse square root of the idele norm of α, which is computed from α·ᾱ·P′(ζ), a unit at every finite place; the product of |v(ϖ_E)| over the infinite places v is rd_E^f.

steps.claim: There are k > 0 and y ∈ E^× such that α^k and the principal idele of y have the same valuation at every finite place and χ_fin(α)^k = ∏_v Φ_v(ȳ), the product over the embeddings Φ_v of the CM type.

It suffices to prove the equality of f-th powers, f = #infinite places of E (both sides are ≥ 0, f ≠ 0): (|σ(s₀)|²)^f = rd_E^f/(√d)^f. The numerator rd_E^f is replaced by ∏_v |v(ϖ_E)| over the infinite places, and the left side is rewritten as |σ(s₀^f)|².
steps.lean:
erw [rootDiscr, ← pow_left_inj₀, div_pow, ← prod_varpi_eq_rootDiscr_pow, pow_right_comm,
    ← norm_pow, ← map_pow]

steps.claim: Since s₀^f = χ_fin(α)⁻¹, the left side is |σ(χ_fin(α))|⁻². Moreover χ_fin(α)^k = ∏_v Φ_v(ȳ) is the norm N_{E/K}(ȳ), an element of K, so σ fixes it; hence |σ(χ_fin(α))|^k = |χ_fin(α)|^k and, k being positive, |σ(χ_fin(α))| = |χ_fin(α)|. The goal becomes |χ_fin(α)|⁻² = ∏_v|v(ϖ_E)|/(√d)^f.
steps.lean:
simp [vacuumRoot, by simpa [h.ne'] using congr(‖$(σ.commutes ⟨chiFin (P.α s) ^ k, by simp_all
    [prod_phi_eq_norm]⟩)‖)]

steps.claim: Computation of |χ_fin(α)|: |υ(α)| = 1, so |χ_fin(α)|⁻² is the idele norm |α|; the idele α·ᾱ·P′(ζ) is a unit at every finite place, so its idele norm is the product over the infinite places of |v(α ᾱ P′(ζ))|², and |v(ϖ_E)| = |v(P′(ζ))|·√d. Together these give the required equality.
steps.lean:
simpa [ideleAbs_toAdele, Finset.prod_pow, infinitePlace_apply_varpi, chiFin, Circle.norm_coe,
    ← InfinitePlace.apply, Finset.prod_nonneg, NeZero.ne, chiAdelic, field] using
    (ideleAbs_eq_prod_of_v_eq_one (x := finIdeleIncl _ * star (finIdeleIncl _) * .map toAdele.1
    (.mk0 _ (P.relDifferentGen_ne_zero s))) (by simpa using v_alpha_mul_relDifferentGen) :)

steps.claim: The side conditions left by step 2 (non-negativity of both sides) hold.
